seo.title: Rabat Travel Guide 2026 | Capital, Udayas Kasbah & Bouregreg Coast | MoroccoTripMap
seo.description: Rabat guide: Kasbah of the Udayas, Hassan Tower, Chellah, medina, Bouregreg marina and Atlantic beach. Practical travel tips and a 3-day itinerary.

name: Rabat
hero_subtitle: Ochre ramparts, a lived-in medina and the quiet pulse of the Bouregreg — the Atlantic capital.

info.area_val: Walled town, ochre brick and Bouregreg calm

overview.title: Welcome to Rabat — Atlantic capital of the Bouregreg
overview.p1: Rabat sits where the Bouregreg meets the Atlantic. Travellers value it as the calm capital for its walls and medina — without the imperial-city intensity. Kasbah of the Udayas organises daily life; the souks and gates reward slow walking.
overview.p2: Two or three days cover the walls, Udayas and the markets; a second morning suits Chellah or a deeper medina wander. Stay inside or near the walls for atmosphere, or use Rabat as a calmer base in the Bouregreg.

places.title: Must-visit places in Rabat
places.subtitle: Kasbah, tower, necropolis, medina and the Bouregreg shore.

oudayas.title: Kasbah of the Udayas
oudayas.desc: White-and-blue quarter above the river mouth with Andalusian gardens.

hassan.title: Hassan Tower
hassan.desc: Iconic Almohad minaret and the esplanade of the unfinished mosque.

mausoleum.title: Mohammed V Mausoleum
mausoleum.desc: Marble and zellige memorial beside Hassan Tower.

chellah.title: Chellah
chellah.desc: Roman and Merinid necropolis in a walled garden by the Bouregreg.

medina.title: Rabat Medina
medina.desc: Compact lanes, souks and the Andalusian wall near the ocean.

gardens.title: Andalusian Gardens
gardens.desc: Shaded gardens inside the Udayas kasbah.

marina.title: Bouregreg Marina
marina.desc: Modern marina and promenade facing Salé across the estuary.

beach.title: Rabat Beach
beach.desc: Atlantic sand below the walls and along the corniche.

museum.title: Museums of Rabat
museum.desc: Archaeology and modern collections in the capital.

itinerary.title: 3 days in Rabat
itinerary.subtitle: Walls and kasbah first, then Hassan Tower & Chellah, then Salé and the waterfront.

detailed_itinerary.day1_m: Morning — Kasbah of the Udayas & Gardens
detailed_itinerary.day1_md: Explore the Kasbah of the Udayas and Andalusian gardens with ocean views.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ad: Wander the medina lanes and Rue des Consuls; enjoy coffee near the sea walls.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ed: Mint tea at Café Maure followed by traditional dinner inside the medina.
detailed_itinerary.day2_md: Visit Hassan Tower esplanade and the marble Mohammed V Mausoleum.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ad: Explore Roman and Merinid ruins nestled inside lush gardens.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ed: Sunset walk along the modern marina facing the lights of Salé.
detailed_itinerary.day3_md: Cross the river by traditional boat to visit Salé's historic medina.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ad: Relax on Rabat beach or enjoy shopping in modern Agdal district cafés.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ed: Final dinner facing the estuary as evening sets in.

stays.title: Where to stay in Rabat? Our Favorites
stays.subtitle: Charming medina riads, luxury hotels in Hassan, and modern apartments in Agdal.

card1.name: Riad Dar Nouzha
card1.desc: Charming sanctuary inside the old medina offering authentic Moroccan hospitality.

card2.name: Hotel Tour Hassan
card2.desc: Luxury stay featuring Moorish architecture, located near key historical monuments.

card3.name: Oudayas Residence
card3.desc: Offers sweeping views over the Bouregreg river mouth and the Kasbah with modern comfort.

card4.name: Agdal Suites
card4.desc: Contemporary options in lively Agdal district, close to shopping, dining, and the train station.

booking_banner.title: Explore All Places to Stay in Rabat

eat.title: Where to eat in Rabat
eat.subtitle: Medina mansions, Kasbah cafés, and contemporary dining in Agdal and Hassan.

dinarjat.title: Dinarjat
dinarjat.desc: Refined Moroccan dining inside a beautifully restored house.

naji.title: Dar Naji
naji.desc: Reliable tagines and salads served in a lively traditional atmosphere.

imprevu.title: L'Imprévu
imprevu.desc: Popular contemporary cuisine in the city centre.

maure.title: Café Maure
maure.desc: Mint tea and pastries with sweeping views over the river estuary.

goeland.title: Le Goéland
goeland.desc: Fresh fish and Atlantic seafood close to the ocean.

tour.title: Tour Hassan Restaurant
tour.desc: Elegant dining next to Hassan Tower and historic monuments.

transport.title: Getting around
transport.desc: The tramway efficiently connects Rabat and Salé. Historic areas are easily explored on foot.

bargain.title: Dress code & visits
bargain.desc: Modest dress is required at the Mausoleum. Standard security checks near official sites.

water.title: Atlantic breeze
water.desc: Ocean breezes keep temperatures mild. Bring a light layer for evening terraces.

daytrips.title: Day trips from Rabat
daytrips.subtitle: Across the Bouregreg or along the Atlantic coastline.

sale.name: Salé
sale.desc: Historic medina and wide beach directly across the Bouregreg river.

casa.name: Casablanca
casa.desc: About 50 minutes by train — Hassan II Mosque and the Corniche.

kenitra.name: Kénitra & Mehdia
kenitra.desc: Surf beaches and nature reserve north of the capital.

q1.question: How many days in Rabat?
q1.answer: Two full days cover main highlights. A third day allows time for Salé and museums.

q2.question: Why visit Rabat?
q2.answer: Rabat offers a calmer capital vibe, UNESCO heritage, and fresh Atlantic ocean air.

q3.question: How do I get to Rabat?
q3.answer: Rabat-Salé Airport (RBA), fast ONCF trains, or the motorway from Casablanca.

q4.question: Best area to stay?
q4.answer: Medina for atmosphere, Hassan for monuments, or Agdal for modern cafés and convenience.
